title: Import progress state must match cursor semantics
summary: If two import modes interpret a cursor differently, they must not share the same progress row or aggregate run key. The state key must include every dimension that changes resume, watermark, window, or counter semantics.
ai_value: Before adding or reusing progress tables for full, differential, archive, retry, or per-window imports, agents should check whether the persisted key matches the meaning of the cursor and counters.

applies_to.ecosystem: agent-built data import and backfill workflows
contexts: one system supports both full backfills and incremental or differential imports
progress rows, run rows, or cursor rows are keyed by a small subset such as tenant and source
operators can start another import mode while a long-running backfill is paused, running, or resumable
a status UI displays processed counts, estimates, cursors, watermarks, or import windows

tools.name: general relational database and job-state store

trigger_signals.description: A progress table or run table is keyed only by source, tenant, account, or job name while code branches on mode, window, partition, archive/current source, or full-versus-incremental behavior.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The persisted key may be too coarse; check whether different modes can overwrite each other's cursor or counters.

trigger_signals.description: Starting a small incremental run makes the denominator jump to all historical records, or makes a full backfill resume from the wrong cursor.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: A mode/window mismatch may have reused the wrong progress row or lower-bound cursor.

trigger_signals.description: Processed counts reset on resume even though the operator-facing window has not changed, or counts accumulate across a new window even though the denominator changed.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Counter semantics are not explicit enough; distinguish per-attempt counters from per-window cumulative counters.

negative_signals.description: All modes intentionally share exactly the same cursor meaning, lower-bound policy, denominator, and counter semantics, and concurrent or interleaved starts are forbidden by a durable lease.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A compact key can be correct when the semantics are truly identical or the system prevents interleaving.

negative_signals.description: The progress row is purely ephemeral display state and is never used for resume, lower-bound selection, committed watermark, deduplication, or operator decisions.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Display-only state has lower corruption risk, though misleading UI can still be harmful.

negative_signals.description: The import can safely recompute progress from immutable committed records and does not persist mutable cursors or counters between attempts.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Some idempotent rerun designs avoid explicit progress state; the trap applies mainly when persisted state influences resume or visibility.

negative_signals.description: Processed-count stillness occurs during a long transaction while the transaction boundary has not committed.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Stillness inside one long transaction is not necessarily a stalled cursor; check transaction and commit boundaries before rewriting progress semantics.

common_wrong_assumptions: One source has one progress row, even if full and incremental imports use different cursor meanings.
Adding import_mode to logs is enough; it also has to be part of persisted uniqueness if it changes resume behavior.
A cursor can serve both as an in-flight deep position and as the committed lower bound for future incremental work.
Processed count is self-explanatory; operators will know whether it means this attempt, this window, or all history.

first_checks.check: List every field that changes import semantics: mode, source family, account or tenant, partition, window start/end, committed watermark, in-flight cursor, archive/current source, and retry attempt. Compare that list with the unique key of progress and aggregate-run state.
first_checks.why: Any missing semantic dimension can let one run overwrite another run's resume state or displayed progress.

first_checks.check: Run a bounded full-or-large window, then start a bounded incremental-or-small window, and verify that each mode's cursor, denominator, and processed count remain isolated.
first_checks.why: The failure often appears only when modes are interleaved, not when each mode is tested alone.
files: staging or reviewed production test plan

first_checks.check: Define counter labels before UI work: per-attempt processed, per-window cumulative processed, all-time imported total, estimated window total, and committed watermark should not share ambiguous names.
first_checks.why: Clear names prevent a resumed run from looking like it lost work or silently expanded scope.

decision_rules.condition: Two import modes can run or resume against the same source but use different lower bounds, cursor formats, source tables, archive/current scopes, or denominators.
decision_rules.then: Add the differentiating dimensions to the persisted progress/run key and migrate existing state forward-only; keep committed watermarks separate from in-flight cursors.

decision_rules.condition: The operator-facing import window is unchanged and a run is resumed after a partial attempt.
decision_rules.then: Continue the per-window processed counter instead of resetting it; reset only when a new window begins, or expose per-attempt and per-window counters separately.

do_not: Do not reuse one progress row for full and incremental imports merely because they target the same destination table.
Do not let a partial or failed run's in-flight cursor become the committed watermark without reconciliation.
Do not fix an inflated denominator only in UI formatting if the underlying state key still allows cursor clobbering.
Do not publish private tenant identifiers, source names, database names, URLs, account IDs, repository paths, or customer data in public lessons.
Do not classify processed-count stillness during one long transaction as a stall until transaction and commit boundaries are checked.
Do not use cursor-key fixes as proof that side effects committed; cross-check watermarks-need-committed-side-effect-evidence for completion-boundary truth.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: When diagnosing import progress or resume bugs, compare cursor semantics to the persisted progress key before changing batch size, retry policy, or UI copy.

risk.notes: Candidate is based on a private production-backed import repair. Promotion needs independent review, especially around migration and live-data handling.

sources.supports: A long-running backfill and a small differential import shared progress state keyed too broadly. Starting the small mode overwrote the large mode's cursor and made estimates look like an all-history sweep. The repair separated state by mode/window, used committed watermarks for incremental lower bounds, and preserved cumulative window counters across resume.
